description.narrative: The program supports Bangladesh's economic recovery from the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic amid a context of heightened regional and global economic uncertainty. Subprogram 2 deepens reforms initiated in subprogram 1, with continued focus in two areas: (i) public financial management (PFM); and (ii) access to finance for the underserved market segments, mainly cottage, micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (CMSMEs). The PFM reforms will help create the fiscal space needed to boost investment in critical physical and social infrastructure. Broadening access to finance will help revitalize CMSMEs, which is crucial not only for preserving employment and livelihoods but also for strengthening production networks throughout the value chain. Subprogram 2 advances these agenda while also building the capacities of government agencies to operationalize the reforms and shaping longer-term reform strategies and plans.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

1.01. The Cabinet approved the new Income Tax Bill for Parliamentary submission that (i) promotes digitization; (ii) simplifies returns; (iii) enhances enforcement by (a) mandating utility services disconnections on failure to pay tax arrears and (b) strengthening Income Tax Appellate Tribunal for tax disputes resolutions; (iv) broadens tax base and reduce loopholes by (a) treating written-off debts as taxable income, (b) treating capital gains from government securities as taxable income, and (c) enforcing income tax return filing by nonresident and digital providers not having permanent establishments in Bangladesh.

1.02. The Ministry of Finance implemented tax collection and compliance measures by (i) enforcing display of proof of tax returns submission in business premises; (ii) introducing penalty measures for tax withholding noncompliance and not disclosing offshore assets; (iii) empowering tax officials to freely access taxpayer's premises and accounts and conduct spot assessments; and (iv) introducing withholding tax rate of 10% for internet services and service delivery agents for mobile financial services.

1.03. The Ministry of Finance (i) implemented gender equality and social inclusion measures in income tax through (a) tax-free annual income limit of TK350,000 for a third-gender assessee (vis-a-vis TK300,000 for a male assessee), (b) tax rebate for an employer employing 10% of its workforce or at least 25 transgender employees or handicapped individuals, and (c) tax exemption for women-owned SMEs having an annual turnover of not more than TK7 million (vis-a-vis the limit of annual turnover of not more than TK5 million for SMEs in general); and (ii) introduced the provision of scheduler filing that removes bias against second earner income in the Cabinet approved new Income Tax Bill.

1.04. To rationalize tax expenditure, mitigate congestion, and promote industrialization in less urbanized areas, the Cabinet approved new Income Tax Bill requires (i) reducing the peak rate of tax exemption by 10 percentage points; and (ii) increasing the average tax exemption rate for new industries outside Dhaka and Chittagong by 8.5 percentage points, and for those inside Dhaka and Chittagong decreasing by 6.0 percentage points.

1.05. To address emerging issues in global taxation and to align the tax regime with international good practices, the Cabinet approved new Income Tax Bill introduced (i) comprehensive treatment of capital gains taxation; (ii) Thin Capitalization Rule imposing deductible interest allowances up to Tk1.5 million in a given fiscal year; and (iii) Transfer Pricing, by constructing a range of acceptable “arm's length pricing” methods for international transactions.
1.06. The NBR implemented electronic deduction of income tax at source for the entire country (all 29 zones) to promote digitalization and improve management of withholding taxes.

1.07. The NBR enforced the proof of income tax returns submission in many business transactions, provided tax incentives for transactions through banks, and reduced rates for One Person Companies to reduce informality and shadow economy activities.

1.08. The NBR (i) implemented fully online VAT registration system with the target of receiving majority of the VAT returns through online system; and (ii) imposed VAT on certain manufacturing products and services to raise VAT revenue collection and prevent leakage.

1.09. The NBR implemented (i) online payment of VAT amounts exceeding Tk5 million; (ii) online payment of income tax for amounts exceeding Tk2 million; and (iii) pilot online personal income tax return filing for income exceeding Tk7 million to improve tax collection efficiency and tax assessment.

1.10. The Ministry of Finance rolled out the policy to deepen Treasury Single Account coverage for 179 Autonomous Bodies strengthening the iBAS++ system to improve efficiency in budget execution and reduce borrowing costs.
1.11. The Ministry of Textiles and Jute privatized five loss-making closed jute mills as part of its SOE reforms to free up scarce public resources.

1.12. The Planning Division, Ministry of Planning implemented the policy for (i) all ministries to incorporate disaster risk and impact assessment in designing projects above Tk500 million to enhance disaster resiliency of public investment; (ii) use of key public investment management tools (Sector Appraisal Format and Ministry Assessment Format) in all economic sectors; and (iii) the use of the digital PPS system for six ministries and/or agencies (Information and Communication Technology Division, Planning Division, Local Government Division, Ministry of Social Welfare, Ministry of Culture, and Ministry of Religion) for development project processing.
1.13. The Cabinet approved the new Public Procurement Authority Bill for Parliamentary submission to streamline procurement and enhance efficiency.

1.14. The Implementation Monitoring and Evaluation Division, Ministry of Planning rolled out the (i) e-CMS of e-GP nationwide; and (ii) digitalized the public procurement method to minimize cost escalations in public contracts, improve contract performance, and enhance the transparency and efficiency of public procurement payments.

1.15. The Finance Division, Ministry of Finance approved the PFM Reform Action Plan (2024-2028) with implementation effective from FY2024, based on the 2022 PEFA Assessment and incorporated gender and climate-related actions to strengthen the PFM system.
